Industry demand reads (Nvidia, Oracle, Nebius selling out and pricing at $40-50M/MW) are strong but already known. I have no edge, so I keep a near-symmetric lognormal centred just under spot ($88) at ~26.5% monthly vol (0.93/sqrt(12)), tilted slightly down for ATM supply. Round 4 (site coverage and split discounting) changes nothing inside the window: the next site deliveries (Dalton Phase 2 from end-2026, Helios II and Bell Saskatchewan in H1-2027) and CoreWeave's Q3 report (expected Nov 5-16) fall after Oct 31, so the 1-month ladder is unchanged.

fair_value.method: Blend of 6.0x Oct-27 NTM EV/EBITDA $100 (40%), 3.0x NTM EV/sales $71 (25%) and a site-level GPU-cohort DCF $9 (35%) = ~$61. The DCF now builds the 4.2 GW contracted site by site (actual rents, ownership, timing), probability-weights the pipeline, refreshes at 0.85k and discounts signed-contract inflows at counterparty rates (IG 7.5%, RPO-weighted 8.4%) and CoreWeave's own lease obligations at 9.25%: floored grid $9.1 split-rate vs $10.9 at a single 11.6% WACC (central cell -$4.8 / +$0.1).

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Site-level GPU-cohort FCFF model, quarterly from 2026-10-01 to 2125, valued at 2026-09-30 and at 2027-09-30 (EV at Oct-27 less modelled Oct-27 net debt $58.5B, over 603M shares). Capacity is built site by site from the inventory: 1,575 MW energized (990 MW at named sites plus 585 MW of company-reported active power at sites with undisclosed MW, allocated by judgment), 350 MW in H2-26, 1,151 MW in 2027 and 1,199 MW in 2028 = the 4.2 GW contracted, each at its own landlord, lease cost, ownership, timing and probability; plus uncontracted pipeline (1.5 GW powered land/options/LOIs at p=0.50; 2.3 GW NVIDIA-framework remainder to 8 GW at p=0.25) valued net of its capex at WACC. Revenue per MW at contract price $10.8M (2025+ vintages; $8.0M for 2023-24 Hopper vintages), calibrated to the $19B exit-2026 run-rate on 1.85 GW. Each cohort: 85% at contract price for 5 yrs (4 for 2023-25 vintages), 15% at market, then 1.00/0.90/0.75/0.66/0.62/0.58/0.54/0.50 of contract price by service year (0.25/0.12/0.06/0.03 after year 8). Capex k=2.4x revenue for new leased capacity, +$7.2M/MW shell capex at owned self-builds (Kenilworth, Hammond, half of powered land), refresh at the economic life L=6y at 0.85k (tech only). Site costs: actual landlord rent ($1.44M/MW-yr Core Scientific, $1.8M Applied Digital, $1.9M Galaxy, $2.2M Blockfusion, $1.8-2.0M others) + power $0.6M/MW-yr (owned: $1.0M ops+power, no rent), +2%/yr; variable 18% of revenue (incl. corporate opex) -> ~59% young-fleet adj. EBITDA margin. SBC 5% of revenue falling to 3% deducted as cash; tax 21% of EBIT from 2029. Split discounting: signed-contract inflows (RPO $103.7B runoff) at counterparty rates (IG 7.5%, Jane Street 8.5%, OpenAI/Anthropic 9.5%, other 10.0%; RPO-weighted 8.4%); CoreWeave's own signed lease obligations at 9.25% (its credit); everything else at WACC 11.6%. Oct-27 per share, k x L grid {2.1/2.4/2.7: 25/45/30%} x {5/6/7y: 25/50/25%}: split rate, each cell floored at $0 = $9.1 (unfloored mean -$9.4; central k2.4/L6 -$4.8); single 11.6% rate floored $10.9 (unfloored -$4.5; central +$0.1). Used: $9.

bear.story: Scarcity eases in 2027-28 as CoWoS supply loosens, Rubin ships in volume and Meta/hyperscalers sell spare capacity. Short-dated $40M/MW deals and the first 2023-25 contracts reprice toward the market index (~0.6x of contract price), capex intensity stays ~2.4-2.7x and net debt passes $58-60B at ~9-10%. Site deliveries slip again (Helios II, the APLD third building, Lancaster), so the exit-2027 run-rate misses $30B while ~$29B+ of rent keeps running: in the runoff case (no refresh, leases paid to term) the DCF is -$8 to -$13. The market prices ~5x EBITDA.

base.story: 2026 lands near $12.8B and 2027 revenue of ~$26B meets consensus. The 2027 sites arrive on their slipped dates, so the exit-2027 run-rate is ~$30B and NTM EBITDA at Oct-27 is ~$20B. Old GPUs keep renting (A100 into 2029), so there is no impairment story, but GAAP losses, SBC, $4B+ interest and refresh capex keep the multiple near 6x NTM EBITDA on ~$58.5B net debt. The stock ends a little below spot. Trimmed from $78 because the site build gives ~3% less NTM EBITDA than round 3's run-rate path.

bull.story: Scarcity lasts through 2027-28 (Nvidia sold out, ~$1T hyperscaler capex) and expiring contracts re-book within ~5%, as the H100s did. Renewals at $40M/MW and prepayments push new-deal capex intensity to ~2.0-2.1x, where the split-rate DCF reaches ~$30-40 at a 6-yr life and the pipeline turns value-creating. The multiple re-rates toward 7-8x EBITDA. Unchanged.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$45 (about half of spot and 26% under the July low of $60.55), equity would be ~$28B on 620M shares against ~$58.5B of Oct-27 net debt: EV ~$86B, ~4.3x NTM EBITDA, below any neocloud peer. Getting there would most likely mean one of three things: an impaired backlog (a cut from Customer A, 40% of H1 revenue), expiring contracts repricing well below the ~0.6x-of-contract market path (a glut, not scarcity), or a failed or punitive refinancing, not ordinary 93%-vol noise. The site work adds two concrete triggers. The first is a second slip of the 2027 deliveries: Helios II, the APLD third building, Lancaster and Dalton P2 are ~660 MW, ~22% of the YE27 >3 GW. The second is evidence that refresh is uneconomic while 12-15-yr rents run on, which is the runoff case (DCF -$8 to -$13). Unchanged at $45: the split-rate DCF moved up from ~$1 to ~$9, but both sit far below the price, which follows the EBITDA multiple.

key_uncertainties: Capex intensity on new deals: at the site level a new leased cohort breaks even near k ~2.3x pre-tax at WACC (~2.4x if its 5-yr contract is IG-backed), against ~2.4-2.6x observed. At k 2.1x the split-rate DCF is ~$35 at a 6-yr life; at 2.7x it is about -$44
Economic life and post-contract repricing: whether expiring contracts re-book near the original price (H100 within 5%, A100 into 2029) or follow the ~0.6x market path once Rubin is plentiful
Delivery: ~1.15 GW is due in 2027 (Helios II already slipped a year; DDTL 3.0 covenants reset for delivery). A 6-month slip of every undelivered site costs ~$4/share of DCF and ~3-5% of NTM EBITDA

reasoning: Round 4 (site coverage + split discounting). I rebuilt the DCF from the site inventory. The 4.2 GW contracted is placed site by site: 1,575 MW energized, 350 MW in H2-26, 1,151 MW in 2027 and 1,199 MW in 2028, each with its landlord rent ($1.44-2.2M/MW-yr), power, ownership, slipped timing and a probability. The 585 MW of active power and 866 MW of contracted power that the inventory cannot tie to a named site are allocated to the rows with undisclosed MW, so each MW appears once. Exited Poolside and the CORZ merger are removed, and no power is used twice (CoreWeave does no mining). The pipeline (1.5 GW powered land at p 0.5; the 2.3 GW NVIDIA-framework remainder at p 0.25) is valued net of its capex at WACC. It is worth -$9.5/share at k 2.4, because new capacity at that intensity earns below WACC. I applied the round-3 supervisor's corrections: refresh at 0.85k instead of the full 2.4k, actual rents instead of a 14% fixed cost, shell capex at owned self-builds (round 3 wrongly assumed every shell was leased), unvested RSUs taken out of the DCF share count, the JV commitments added, and the 2025 capex corrected to the ~$21.1B accrual figure. Bridge at k 2.4/L6, as cumulative Oct-27 values per share: round 3 -$108. Re-basing to the site engine gives -$64, because round 3 also refilled post-contract decay at full k and grew 3% a year with growth capex. The remaining steps run to -$8 (refresh at 0.85k), -$2 (actual rents), -$13 (owned shells), +$1 (probability weights), +$1 (RSU fix; equity is near zero so the share count barely matters), $0 (JV), +$3 (split rate on contracted inflows) and -$4.8 (lease obligations at CoreWeave's 9.25% credit). Split discounting: signed-contract inflows (RPO $103.7B) are discounted at counterparty rates anchored on DDTL 4.0's ~5.9% (IG 7.5%, OpenAI 9.5%, RPO-weighted 8.4%). That adds ~$4/share. Applying the same rule to the leases, where CoreWeave is the Ba3 payer, puts $29B+ of rent at 9.25% and costs ~$9/share. So the split-rate DCF is slightly below the single-rate one: floored grid $9.1 vs $10.9, central -$4.8 vs +$0.1. The firm's rent obligations run longer and are firmer than its IG customer contracts are large. Fair value is unchanged at ~$61: the DCF rose ($1 -> $9) and the multiples fell ($104 -> $100, $76 -> $71) on ~3% lower site-timed NTM revenue. Scenarios are trimmed (bear $35, base $76) and the median falls ~$1 to ~$74.5. P(>=89) is 0.378 (from 0.384); sigma 0.69 and 6% distress mass are unchanged. The 1-month ladder and the $45 thesis break are unchanged. Research this round: two primary checks (the DDTL 4.0 deck and SEC XBRL company facts for PP&E, RPO, leases and the VIE). The site facts are taken from the checked inventory and its landlord sources. No web searches.

discounting.basis: Rates in % a year; DCF values in $/share at 2027-10-01 (k x L grid, each cell floored at $0). Contracted rate = RPO-weighted rate on cash flows inside signed customer contracts: IG 7.5% (Meta Aa3/AA-, NVIDIA Aa1/AA backstop, Microsoft Aaa; ~55% of RPO), Jane Street 8.5% (Fitch BBB-, Moody's Ba1; ~6%), OpenAI/Anthropic 9.5% (unrated; DDTL 3.0 at SOFR+400; ~23%), other 10.0% (DDTL 5.0 SOFR+450 class; ~16%). The IG anchor is DDTL 4.0: A3, non-recourse, ~5.9% fixed (SOFR+225), 90% LTC, 1.2x DSCR (~102% LTC), fully amortising against the Meta contract; +~160bp for the residual above debt service and for completion/operating risk. CoreWeave's own signed rent obligations to landlords (Core Scientific, Galaxy, Applied Digital, Blockfusion and others; CoreWeave pays) are discounted at 9.25%, its unsecured credit cost, matching APLD's 9.25% notes secured on CoreWeave leases. Post-contract, uncontracted, pipeline, refresh and terminal cash flows stay at the 11.6% WACC. Effect at k2.4/L6: contracted inflows +$4.2/share, lease leg -$9.1/share, so the split DCF sits below the single-rate one (central -$4.8 vs +$0.1; unfloored grid mean -$9.4 vs -$4.5). Inflows alone, without the lease leg, would give a floored $12.8. Used in fair value: split-rate $9. Site values in site_coverage are EV contributions at Oct-27 for the central cell (k 2.4, L 6, split rate). They sum to $92.2/share; less net debt incl. JV ($97.1/share on 603M) that gives the central -$4.8. Sites whose capex is mostly spent before Oct-27 show higher values because that capex already sits in net debt.
